world.bio: I'm Rachel Weiss, a registered psychotherapist (RP) in private practice in Toronto's Annex. I mostly see couples, evenings, in a rented office on Bloor. I trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy and have been practising for eleven years. My daughter just started at McGill and calls every night.
skills_assets: Registered psychotherapist (CRPO), 11 years in private practice
Trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) for couples
A rented two-room office on Bloor Street, month-to-month lease
Referral relationships with a psychiatrist and two family doctors
A small waiting list of about eight couples

projects.name: Sliding-scale day
projects.text: I've been thinking about adding one day a week at reduced fees for couples who can't afford my standard rate. I'd need to cover costs; a sliding scale of $60-120 per session. The problem is my landlord has told me he wants to raise the office rent by 18 percent starting in January, which makes the math harder.

projects.name: Muskoka cottage dock
projects.text: The family cottage dock has rotted. Got two quotes, $14,000 and $18,000. My husband wants to wait until spring, I'd like it done before the ice. We keep postponing the conversation.

notes.text: Back-to-back sessions tonight. One couple argued about whose mother is more intrusive. Afterwards I sat in the dark for ten minutes. I've learned to leave the work at the door, but some evenings it follows me down Bloor.

Plantar fasciitis again. The podiatrist says rest and stretching, no running for six weeks. I miss the morning run along the ravine more than I'd admit. Bought a foam roller and a frozen water bottle for my heel.

Landlord's email: rent up 18 percent from January. I replied politely, then spent an hour drafting a sharper one I did not send. I should look at other spaces, but moving a practice is its own kind of grief for clients.
Maya called at 11pm from her dorm. Homesick, misses my cooking, her roommate plays music late. We talked for forty minutes. I wanted to say 'come home' and said 'it gets easier' instead.

Supervision group. Presented a case about a couple where one partner won't speak in session. The group suggested I stop trying to make him speak. I'd forgotten how freeing it is to be told what I already know.
Cottage weekend, rainy. The dock is worse than I thought; one plank went through under my foot. David says spring. I said the ice will take it. We both went quiet.
Thinking about the sliding scale again. If the rent goes up, I either raise fees or take a loss. Neither feels right. Maybe I find another therapist to share the space on the day I'm there.
Dinner with an old friend from my master's program. She left clinical work for corporate EAP. 'Better hours,' she said. I pretended to consider it.
Rosh Hashanah at my sister's. Her husband asked what I do exactly and then told me about his divorce. Every family dinner I'm a free therapist whether I want to be or not.
Cleaned out the winter closet. Found Maya's old skates. Kept them.

messages.text:
David: Landlord email again?
Me: Yes. 18 percent.
David: We can absorb it for a year.
Me: It's not about absorbing it.

Maya: Mom, midterms start next week.
Me: You'll be fine.
Maya: You always say that.
Me: Because it's always true.

Okafor: Would you consider sharing office hours? I'm looking for space two days a week.
Me: Possibly. Let me check the lease.

Podiatrist: Keep up the stretching. No running yet.
Me: I'm walking at least.
Podiatrist: Walking is fine.

Dana: Are you coming for the holiday dinner?
Me: Yes, bringing dessert.
Dana: Not your apple cake again.
Me: It is my apple cake.
